messages:
amanda: Heads up — ran a full canary perf run against the kernel-mapping change. Seeing a surprising tail increase on the generation (decode) phase despite overall token throughput being fine. posted flame graphs + diffs: https://perf.internal/runs/3968000000 :eyes:
perf-bot: perf-alert: redwood-x-14q decode-stage p99 latency +37% vs baseline. job=canary-3968, build=kernel-mapping-v3
raj: Can you paste the main numbers? p50/p95/p99 + throughput impact?
amanda: quick snapshot from the run:
```
model: redwood-x-14q
workload: 80% small-gen (<=64t), 20% long prefill (~256t)
baseline -> experiment (kernel-mapping-v3)
prefill: p50 18ms -> 19ms, p95 40ms -> 42ms, p99 120ms -> 125ms
decode: p50 10ms -> 13ms (+30%), p95 35ms -> 48ms (+37%), p99 110ms -> 150ms (+36%)
throughput tokens/sec: 1.02M -> 0.99M (-3%)
kv-cache hit: 96% -> 87% (notable drop)
hot kernels: attention_dense_fast (used for prefill), attention_sparse_fallback (now used more in decode for short sequences)
kernel_switches/request: +44% (more fallbacks)
```
oliver: Interesting — kernel mapping v3 is picking the sparse fallback for many short-gen batches. That fallback has worse latency at small sequences on current CUDA kernels. We should prefer attention_dense_fast for seq<=64 at decode even if its FLOP efficiency is lower; latency matters for p99. Also avoid mixing prefill and gen in the same batch shape — split batch formation by phase.
sara: Adding to that, KV thrash looks correlated: when we split batches mid-request across queues the KV priming is getting evicted. We lose locality. Idea: tag small-gen requests as KV-hot and extend KV-priming window to 15ms for them so they stay resident through the handshake.
ben: Pragmatic plan: 1) separate queues for prefill vs generation with independent batching windows, 2) decode token-budget target set lower (e.g. targetTokens=32) to keep decode batches compact, 3) prefer low-latency kernel for gen by explicit kernel-hint rule. I'll spin a canary with those three knobs.
amanda: I pushed a branch: https://git.redwood/r/2345 — includes kernel-hint rule (seq<=64 -> dense_fast), queue split, decode token target 32, kv-priming extension gated behind flag. Can @perf-bot schedule microbench?
perf-bot: scheduled: microbench-canary-3968000028 (1M small-gen requests, 100k large-prefill). ETA ~5m.
oliver: Also request we add two metrics to dashboards before the canary: kernel_switches_per_request and kv_warm_hit_latency. Need to be able to correlate switch spikes to tail.
raj: If the canary shows p99 improvement but slight throughput regression, we should consider soft-fallback logic: prefer new mapping but fall back to old kernel if p99 exceeds threshold for a customer tier.
amanda: Agreed. I'll collect traces + flamegraphs after the run and post them here. If this looks good we can roll to night window with a circuit-breaker. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
ben: I'll follow up with a short A/B that toggles only the kernel-hint to measure pure kernel effect.
sara: quick note — watch KV memory pressure on the node during the microbench, the priming window increase might increase resident KV size briefly.
amanda: noted. will attach node memory graphs. back in ~10m with results.
